key_insight: Trigonal selenium is intrinsically defect tolerant: even though point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic losses.
engineering_relevance: This points to t-Se as a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering focused more on device integration and doping control than on eliminating recombination hotspots.
method: First-principles calculations of defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination in trigonal selenium
Survey of a large, chemically diverse set of point defects and charge states
Comparison of nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture under different doping conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a broad computational evaluation showing large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, which strongly suppress recombination despite multiple deep defect levels.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on idealized first-principles defect modeling, so real-device losses may still involve extrinsic defects, interfaces, or processing-related nonidealities not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
